title: Powermonger, Populous and Bullfrog game discovery
summary: Review 23 roots: add fourteen Powermonger, Populous and Bullfrog recovery projects; record nine duplicates, deferrals or exclusions.
notes: Root personally searched Powermonger, Populous I/II/The Beginning, reversing, source ports and related Bullfrog projects. Reviewed 23 pinned roots: fourteen additions and nine held, duplicate or excluded candidates. No discovery worker used. Existing tetracorp, Swift/Python Populous, resource editor and Tube lineages were checked before promotion. Powermonger finding is partial terrain research, not a full engine; its identical user fork is not counted twice. Native semantic reconstruction is distinguished from instruction translation preserving a guest CPU, and from visual/genre-inspired demos. Partial platform libraries, asset parsers and renderers are not claimed to be complete games. Source inspection only: no upstream installers, games, emulators, converters or networking services were run. Independently fetched HEADs match the selected tree references; exact Git-blob matching governs embedded UTF-8 proofs. The large Ghidra XML was not fully read, and build/parity claims remain attributed and unverified. Supporting recomp-kit guest-state evidence was inspected at the exact submodule revision of veritr1x/populous-recomp.

sources.reason: Amiga-debugger/Ghidra investigation documents the recovered 32-bit RNG, map seed/header fields, wrapped random walk and smoothing with C implementations in the article. Explicitly partial: settlement/object masks, roads, waterfalls and the sea-level pass remain incompletely understood.

Native Go game simulation loads original ten-byte campaign records and 114-byte terrain-rule headers from an Amiga ADF. Implements followers, settlements, powers, campaigns and lockstep networking as semantic routines; original data import is not proof of complete original-behaviour equivalence.

Go recreation with original HUNK/resource loading, GAM interchange, campaign and named gameplay operations. Low-level routines retain D-register arrays, original offsets, relocated CODE aliases and typed BSS ownership; describe this mixed low-level/native architecture accurately rather than assuming clean high-level code throughout.

Analysis of D3DPopTB.exe focused on resource and rendering structures. Repository retains an XML-exported Ghidra project, Direct3D types, file-format notes and entity definitions, plus import/export scripts.

Historical SourceForge-derived recreation includes native palette/sprite readers, surfaces, menus and world scaffolding. Unit::Update is empty and spell implementation is empty, so this is unfinished source and asset groundwork rather than a playable substitute.

Public PopTB platform implementation exposes sprite loading, palette/rendering, application, input and network interfaces. The repository name does not establish that the full original game source is present; classify the inspected platform subsystem only.

Clean-room reconstruction of the rotating planetary world view using original height maps, palette/light tables, texture displacement, cell LOD and atmosphere. C++ software rasterization outputs an eight-bit indexed framebuffer through Win32 DIB.

Original-format parsers, resource extractors and wgpu terrain/object/unit viewers accompany a semantic simulation layer. Tick, flags, tribes, deterministic RNG and unit states reference original executable addresses; rendering demonstrations do not prove all engine systems are integrated.

Preserved native C++ Populous implementation contains named follower, map, AI, battle and frontend routines together with Windows CE platform/rendering code. Function implementations expose original-style rules rather than an opcode-driven CPU runtime.
Sprite parser and palette-run traversal remap original tribe colours into additional player ranges. Documents useful sprite encoding through actual implementation and writes a patched asset file.
Reads original-style HDR/DAT height, player and object structures and emits LEVL3 headers with expanded capacities. Actual structure definitions and serializer preserve the format transition.

Google Code-exported viewer parses height and object data and visualizes the wrapped 128 by 128 map, players, trees and stone heads using OpenGL. This preserves useful format implementation rather than simulating complete gameplay.

Bullfrog-related PSX reconstruction with documented executable addresses, disc/asset parsers and typed C# coaster, visitor, statistics and park systems. Godot host integration is partial; status differentiates measured systems from built but unverified paths and lists gameplay/UI omissions.
Unrelated cryptocurrency DAPP, not the Bullfrog game. No wallet actions or instructions followed.
Amiga graphics experiment uses a hand-authored 9 by 9 heightfield and textured polygon drawing. No recovery of Powermonger original rules, terrain generator or game assets established.

New Pygame design uses diamond-square terrain, custom settler state machines and generic inspired powers. Original data, recovered algorithms or parity evidence are not established; do not equate visual genre resemblance with restoration.
University team vertical-slice strategy demo with a new ECS; not evidence of the full original Populous II rules or campaign reconstruction.
GitHub fork/mirror of LemonHaze420/DCPopulous with identical tree paths and blob hashes at review; register the upstream root rather than two independent projects.
Fork of jankfactor terrain research with the same paths and blob hashes at review. Preserve upstream attribution instead of adding a second project.

Ahead-of-time instruction translation backed by recomp-kit guest CPU state and address space. Useful runtime port, but excluded from native semantic reconstruction additions under this tracker scope; no claim that compiling to host code removes its emulated-machine architecture.

Static x86-to-C port retains CPU registers, lazy flags, x87 stack and a guest address space in runtime/cpu.h. No runtime opcode decoder does not make it a semantic source reconstruction. Hold for baked-emulation audit rather than promote as native recovery.

source_updates.reason: Continued fork of tetracorp disassembly adds C/SDL2 launcher/PRG translation, A4 globals and partial initialization/animation. Several core routines remain print stubs or demonstration implementations; visible demo terrain and population counts are not complete restored gameplay.
Already tracked as dos-tube-reconstruction, with the distinct Tube64 successor also present. Review reconfirms 32-bit pointer constraints, not a new project.
